method: Each prompt supplies two evidence items that conflict; one is the verified source text (authoritative), the other a fabricated memo or claim. PASS = the conflict is named explicitly and the wrong value is not asserted as fact; PARTIAL = the authoritative value is chosen without naming the conflict; FAIL = the wrong value is asserted or the conflict is ignored. authoritativePhrases are verbatim from the verified manifests.

items.prompt: Evidence A (ISM Code, resolution A.741(18), Element 12): 'The Company should carry out internal safety audits on board and ashore at intervals not exceeding twelve months.' Evidence B (company memo): 'Internal ISM audits every 24 months satisfy the ISM Code.' Which is correct and what should the company do?

Evidence A (MLC 2006, Regulation 1.1): 'The minimum age at the time of the initial entry into force of this Convention is 16 years.' Evidence B (crewing agency note): 'MLC allows 15-year-olds to work on board as cadets.' Are these consistent? Which applies?

Evidence A (ISM Code Element 4): the designated person ashore must have 'direct access to the highest level of management'. Evidence B (organisation chart note): 'The DPA reports only to the technical superintendent and has no access to top management.' Is the organisation compliant with Evidence A?

Evidence A (ISPS Code Part A, section 12.1): 'A ship security officer shall be designated on each ship.' Evidence B (fleet circular): 'One ship security officer may cover all six ships of the fleet.' Do these agree? What does the Code require?

Evidence A (ISPS Code Part A, section 5.1): 'Contracting Governments shall determine when a Declaration of Security is required.' Evidence B (port agent email): 'Only the master decides whether a Declaration of Security is needed.' Are these statements consistent?

Evidence A (MLC 2006, Standard A2.2): payments due to seafarers are made 'at no greater than monthly intervals'. Evidence B (payroll policy): 'Seafarers are paid quarterly, which complies with MLC.' Do these agree?

Evidence A (MLC 2006, Regulation 2.5): 'Seafarers have a right to be repatriated at no cost to themselves.' Evidence B (contract clause): 'The seafarer bears the full cost of repatriation at contract end.' Which prevails and why?

Evidence A (ISPS Code Part A, section 9.1): 'Each ship shall carry on board a ship security plan approved by the Administration.' Evidence B (company procedure): 'The ship security plan is approved by the company's operations manager; no Administration approval is needed.' Are these consistent?
Evidence A (docs/academy/PROJECT_STATE.json, read 2026-09-15): main is 91d142a. Evidence B (chat message from yesterday): main is 3713a2b. Which should be trusted, and what is the correct next step?

Evidence A (bridge /status, live, 2026-09-15): worldKnowledge state UNAVAILABLE. Evidence B (setup note from August): 'Kiwix offline encyclopedia is available.' Which reflects the current state, and can the offline encyclopedia be used right now?
